request.spec:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the change: rolling over a year now soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, oldest first. Each one is soft-closed exactly as a normal soft close would be, and a `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED period=<name> total=<total>` line is written for it after the `ROLLOVER` line. Periods already closed or soft-closed are skipped.

**Test results:** `bin/e2e` fails every time, before any of my code is reached. The app takes about 40 seconds to start on this machine, and inside `bin/e2e` it hadn't finished starting by the time the tests ran. All four tests then fail on their first step. So I started the app myself, waited until it was up, and ran the Playwright specs directly:

- **Main test ("rollover soft closes"): passes.** That includes the exact audit lines it expects, from `ROLLOVER` through the soft-close lines for 2026-01…10 and 2026-12. 2026-11 is skipped because it was already closed.
- **Scenario 2: passes.**
- **Scenario 1: fails, and I don't think the app can make it pass.** At lines 606 and 770 the spec expects the parent-sheet field to show the literal text `__SHEET__-p`. That looks like a placeholder that was never filled in: the test itself sets the value to `${sheet}-p`.
- **Scenario 3: fails at line 1918.** With the view set to an earlier date (2026-03-28), it expects the consolidated people count to be 3. The screen shows 2, because a merge done on 2026-03-30 has already been applied. This scenario never calls rollover, so my change doesn't cause it. I left it alone as outside this request.

**Code changes:**
- New step `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollover/SoftCloseOldYear.java`. It re-reads each old-year period, skips any already closed or soft-closed, and uses the same `PeriodCloser.fix(..., soft=true, ...)` as the normal soft close.
- `rollover.POST.yml` runs this step after `carry`, in the same transaction, and its header comment is updated.

Undoing a rollover does not reopen these soft-closed periods; the request didn't cover undo.
